dialogueHistory.line: Rexx: Well, not exactly. But we can get you set up on Facebook Marketplace, TikTok Shop, Whatnot, and other places. You can do live shopping, too. But first, let’s start right here. Take photos of everything you have in here and let BizBox inventory it for you. We’ll get you some boxes. After you photograph each item, put it in the right box. BizBox tells you what number to write on it. Then close it up. Now you know what’s in each box and where everything is. We keep going until it’s all organized and easy to get to. Once that’s done, we’ll put together your script for live shopping. But all you have to do for now is take the photos.

sections.title: 1. Start here: assignments and sources
steps: Select the assigned scene and inspect status, quality holds, notes and approved frame IDs. A hold means review/preparation only; do not render.
Use approved character, outfit, prop and environment references on this storyboard. Open the actual original images; newest filename or thumbnail does not equal approval.
Record source filenames and SHA256 where available. Assign one worker per candidate asset. Do not overwrite the approved source or other scenes.
Use exact dialogue and voice takes from the scene card. Missing fields are gaps to resolve, not permission to invent lines or timing.

sections.title: 2. Image quality: prevent and reject drift
steps: Start from the identified approved original-resolution master. Never use a rejected candidate, browser screenshot or upscaled delivery as a new edit master.
Bound the edit to a visible region. Use a real local mask if supported; saying preserve everything is not a pixel lock.
Show clutter through object placement, not dirty or grungy texture. Preserve real dark objects, shadows and marker lettering; reject artificial black stains or smeared seams.
Compare changed AND untouched areas at native pixels. Check body/head/neck size, pose, hands, hair, door paint, packaging counts, box labels and occlusion. Never move people to expose lettering.
Reject unwanted changes and return to the approved source. Stop whole-image retries after two failures at the same correction and propose another method.
Measure actual output dimensions. Label resampled deliveries as 8K upscaled; enlargement does not restore missing detail. Review artifacts before enlargement.

sections.title: Video input gate · native clarity and matching frames
steps: Read shared-skills/rexx-still-continuity/SKILL.md, including Required video input check, before preparing video inputs. Record videoInputReview on the scene with exact start/end IDs and source/delivery SHA256 hashes, native dimensions, reviewer, findings and owner approval evidence. Missing or held review blocks submission; changed hashes require a new review.

Inspect native images at 100% and intended video crop before 8K delivery export. Reject soft skin, mottled or patterned plain-black shirts, artificial black stains, smeared hands and panel edges. A sharp thumbnail or 7680x4320 file is not proof of native detail. An 8K upscale cannot repair these defects.

For a fixed-camera shot, start from one approved frame and change only the requested actor/action. Compare door corners, panel grid, seams, paint, perspective and stationary people at matching coordinates. No added zoom, push-in or independently invented set geometry. For different camera angles, verify rigid-set continuity or use separately directed shots and a cut.

Keep action beats separate: entrance greeting has closed door and unpressed remote; the following shot contains the press and slow opening. Use an actual accepted video endpoint for the next clip; never a distorted endpoint.

Run node assert-render-inputs.cjs on actual upload files to block rejected paths and hashes, including upscaled derivatives. This is not a visual-quality detector. A pass still requires native clarity, geometry and approval checks.

Do not retry a failed pair merely by adding stronger negative wording. Record observed failure and uncertainty, hold the setup, and change the method. After two unsuccessful whole-frame attempts at a localized edit, stop and use a supported local method or propose a cut. No automatic paid rerenders.

sections.title: 3. Higgsfield: prepare the multi-shot
steps: Use the signed-in Higgsfield video page and exact scene model/settings. Use fixed-camera or multi-shot mode only as specified by the current scene; no default multi-shot or camera movement. Inspect current controls.
Open the linked scene multi-shot manifest. Upload its actual first frame as Start image. Remove stale previous-scene inputs from the form.

For a multi-shot scene, upload only its current approved, reviewed shot references as separately named Elements and select/tag them in their corresponding shots. For a continuous start/end shot, load the reviewed pair. Do not reuse retired GARAGE-03 reveal footage or old manifests. Typed @text is not proof of an attachment.
Use the linked 8K upscaled file if accepted by upload; retain original masters as fallback. Set-only image is supplemental, never an empty-of-people action shot.

Set durations from approved action/dialogue timing. Garage 4+3+3 seconds is a visual proposal, not verified speech timing. Preserve approved voices for editing; do not generate invented dialogue or captions.

Verify all thumbnails/tags, starting image, prompts, shot order, duration, resolution, model and displayed credit cost before submitting. Respect scene holds and actual direct-confirmation requirements. Do not duplicate an uncertain paid request.
Record job ID, source URL, cost, settings and observed status on the scene. A prepared form is not a queued render. No recurring monitoring or automatic retries.
Save the completed original MP4; verify duration, streams and decode/playback. Review continuity. A browser playing a video is not a saved file. Record local and verified Drive locations.

sections.title: 4. Audio and completed scenes
steps: Reuse exact approved voice takes. Fit speaking durations before rendering and verify lip-sync afterward.
Finish each rebuilt scene with dialogue, effects and audience cues before advancing. Keep voices, effects, audience and music separately editable.
Audience reactions follow the reveal or punchline and stay below dialogue. Follow the owner cues recorded on the scene.
Short music excerpts have no guaranteed safe duration. Use audio cleared for the intended posting and record its source/rights; do not promise that a few seconds prevents a claim.
The coordinator inserts reviewed clips and updates storyboard timing, media and approval state. The full-episode pass handles overall loudness, transitions and music balance.

sections.title: 5. Roles and sharing
steps: Image worker: return one candidate with prompt, exact input IDs, output dimensions and inspection findings. No automatic approval, storyboard replacement or paid render.
Reviewer: independently compare source/candidate and report specific defects. Do not silently regenerate or replace.
Coordinator: owns active selections, approvals, archives, audio, assembly and authorized render submission.
Use lower-cost coordination models when suitable and available. Image-generation access and billing are separate; do not assume lower chat cost makes images free.
Export instructions from this live storyboard and attach the actual references for other chats. Verify GitHub/Drive sharing before claiming another agent has access.

stillResolutionRequirement.ownerEvidence: the still image should always be8K; give the image rendering to agents here

coordination.coordinator: One coordinator owns the active storyboard, approvals, integration and final render submission.
coordination.workers: Start bounded workers only for current independent tasks. Supply exact attached references and scene export; close workers after their result and receipt are saved.
coordination.durableRecords: Keep scripts, scene metadata, hashes, approval evidence and task state in the GitHub project when synchronized. Local edits are not automatically pushed.
coordination.media: Keep large media on D: and verified cloud backups. GitHub records asset links, hashes and versions; it is not a substitute for local RAM or a verified media backup.
coordination.sharing: Workers in other apps need explicit repository/media access and exact attachments. Do not assume automatic cross-app context sharing.

sharedRepository.rule: This shared branch is the working production record. Pull before starting; coordinator commits reviewed changes. Local snapshots are working copies, not independent authorities.
sharedRepository.media: Bundled identity references are listed in CANONICAL-INPUTS.json. Other media dependencies require separate verified transfer.

offerMessagingPolicy.primaryCTA: Sign up for a free demo
offerMessagingPolicy.pricingRevealStage: Not yet specified by owner; do not invent a public price reveal or expose internal rates in lead-generation copy.
offerMessagingPolicy.rule: Use the same three internal tiers across offers. Public ads, landing pages and lead-generation CTAs invite the free demo without displaying prices. Each offer has its own relevant demo and pitch deck.

subscription.model: Software as a service with onboarding
subscription.priceVisibility: internal only; demo-first public flow remains in force
subscription.relationshipToSetup: Recurring software fee in addition to the selected template or setup tier
notYetDefined: billing unit when a customer has multiple offers
subscription.noImpliedPromise: Do not describe support as unlimited, human 24/7 or a guaranteed response time without defined terms.

approvalAssemblyLoop.ownerInstruction: As agents finish, review and approve each result, then update the storyboard and main video together.
approvalAssemblyLoop.workerOutput: Exact scene ID, actual reference inputs/hashes, candidate or approved state, video and editable audio stems where available, source timings and transition notes.
steps: Review actual returned asset against approved character and set references
Record owner approval with its precise scope
For an approved still, update the chosen frame and produce the matching video; do not call the video replaced yet
For approved motion, synchronize approved dialogue, effects, audience/music and adjacent transitions
Export and decode the updated episode; inspect changed boundaries and check audio sync
Update currentFullCut, currentAssembly, runtime and scene-highlight timestamps to the same verified export
Sync the storyboard and production checkpoint to shared GitHub; retain prior versions in history
qualityChecks: Character build, head/neck, tan, hair and wardrobe
Fixed car/set geometry and correct props
No artificial black splotches or warped labels
No duplicate beats, still holds substituting motion, clipped sound or abrupt unintended cuts

Clearly exposed BLACK sock bands between cuffed loose Dickies and Grinch shoes. Plain black oversized XL shirt, beard/glasses. No old walk-up body.

rejectedAssetPolicy.rule: Archive is for recovery/provenance only. Do not use any listed original path, archive path, or SHA256 as a future image/video generation input. V17 recipe may read its archived V16 source only to reproduce the existing composite, never as a new render selection.

videoInputGate.status: Required before new candidate upload or video submission
videoInputGate.limitation: Human/agent visual review is required; no automatic guarantee that a model will preserve pixels or motion.

productionGuide.performanceDirection: Understated reactions: minimal head and hand movement; natural blinking, small eye/lip changes; no broad laughter, chin lifts, theatrical surprise or exaggerated facial acting unless the owner requests that exact beat. Preserve the approved subtle pointing/cross-eyed final payoff.
